### Data table
Rows of records in a scrolling table with a sticky header, sort state and row selection.

Component ID: `data-table`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `shared-runtime`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: A contacts screen where people tap a name to open a profile is a list. A data table would add column headers and sorting nobody uses on a phone.

#### Contract

A `.data-table` is a `<div>` around one native `<table>`. The wrapper scrolls and draws the outline, so the table keeps its table semantics. The header row sticks to the top of the wrapper once the wrapper scrolls vertically, so give the wrapper a `max-block-size` for long tables. Add `numeric` to the header and body cells of a number column to align them on the end edge with tabular figures, and `dense` to the wrapper for shorter rows.

Put a `<button>` in each sortable `<th>` and set `aria-sort="ascending"` or `"descending"` on the header of the sorted column. The framework draws the arrow. Add `data-sort` to the wrapper and the framework sorts too: a header button reorders the rows by its column and moves `aria-sort`. A `numeric` header compares numbers (`$1,200.00` after `$87.00`); other columns compare text in the page's language, with 9 before 10. A cell's `data-value` stands in for its text, and a `tr.data-table-detail` moves with its row. Each press fires a cancelable `expressive:sort` from the wrapper with `{ header, column, direction }`; a server-paged table cancels it and loads the sorted page, with `aria-sort` already moved. Without `data-sort`, the page reorders the rows and moves `aria-sort` itself.

Add a labelled `input[type="search"][data-table-filter]` inside the wrapper for text filtering, and put `data-filter` on each searchable single-column header. A named `output[data-table-filter-count]` with `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` receives the matching record count. Filtering keeps record details together and preserves author-hidden rows. Select-all changes only enabled records visible in the current view, while hidden records keep their selections. Each edit fires cancelable `expressive:filter` with `{ query }`. Cancel synchronously for server filtering, then replace records, write the count and call `Expressive.DataTables.sync(wrapper)`. Sync stays silent and preserves server records and counts until the next uncanceled input; otherwise it reapplies the local query.

#### Syntax

```html
<div class="data-table" data-sort>
  <table>
    <caption>Orders</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th scope="col" aria-sort="ascending"><button type="button">Customer</button></th>
        <th scope="col">Status</th>
        <th scope="col" class="numeric"><button type="button">Total</button></th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <th scope="row">Alvin</th>
        <td>Shipped</td>
        <td class="numeric">$87.00</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <th scope="row">Shannon</th>
        <td>Pending</td>
        <td class="numeric">$9.99</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</div>
```

#### Rules

- `data-table-wraps-the-table`: Put .data-table on a <div> around the <table>. The wrapper scrolls; a table made to scroll itself needs display:block, which drops its table role in some engines.
- `data-table-sort-is-on-a-header`: aria-sort belongs on the column header cell (<th>), not on the button inside it or on a data cell. Assistive technology reads the sort state from the header.
- `data-table-row-is-not-selected`: aria-selected is not valid on a row of a plain table. It belongs to role="grid" and its keyboard contract. Select a row with a labelled checkbox in its first cell.
- `data-table-scroll-region-is-a-region`: A focusable scroll wrapper needs role="region" so its name is announced. aria-label is not allowed on a plain div.
- `data-table-scroll-region-is-named`: Name a focusable scroll wrapper with aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing at the table caption, so keyboard users know what they are scrolling.
- `data-table-filter-is-named`: Give the table search input a label identifying the records it filters.
- `data-table-filter-count-is-named`: Name the result count, for example aria-label="Matching records", so its number has context.
- `data-table-filter-count-is-status`: Give the table result count role="status" so changes are announced without moving focus.
- `data-table-filter-count-is-polite`: Use aria-live="polite" on the table result count so typing does not interrupt other speech.
- `data-table-page-size-is-select`: Use a native select for an authored table page-size control. The existing FormSelect enhancement reads and updates that same select.
- `data-table-page-size-is-single`: A table has one page size. Omit multiple from its page-size select.
- `data-table-page-size-is-named`: Label the table page-size select, for example Rows per page. Option values do not name the control.
- `data-table-page-control-is-button`: Use a native button with type="button" for a local table page control. Ordinary pagination links keep their navigation behavior.
- `data-table-page-control-is-named`: Name each table page button, for example Previous or Next, using visible text or an accessible label.
- `data-table-page-control-is-in-pagination`: Put local table page buttons in a named nav.pagination inside their table wrapper.
- `data-table-page-navigation-is-named`: Name the table's pagination navigation so it is distinct from other navigation on the page.
- `data-table-page-direction-is-known`: Set data-table-page to previous or next. Local table paging does not generate numbered page controls.
- `data-table-page-status-is-named`: Name the page status, for example aria-label="Pages", so its numbers have context.
- `data-table-page-status-is-status`: Give the table page status role="status" so page changes are announced without moving focus.
- `data-table-page-status-is-polite`: Use aria-live="polite" on the table page status so page changes do not interrupt other speech.
